cells.tense: The stance is steady right now, and you can read its pattern while you are inside it.
cells.act: carry on with the version you chose through another week of doubt
cells.ask: Go another week on the decision you already made. If doubt turns up, don't reopen the question — keep to what you chose and watch what holds.
cells.core:
You're standing under something that takes effort and gets no ceremony, and the standing is steady. What shows here is that you can read the shape of it while you're inside it — the load, the way you spread it, what it costs in hours. That read usually arrives after. You have it mid-stride, and there is slack in the middle of the days where you have it. A long-held thing doing the distance tends to look like this: plain work first, nothing lit, then the light, on a schedule nobody scheduled.

Endurance doesn't wait for another sign. It continues a decision already made, with doubt running alongside and no vote in the outcome. Keep what you chose before the doubt came, one more week, and let doubt be scenery rather than a ruling. No further proof needed, no midnight re-litigating. The shape stays readable so long as you keep walking through it.
cells.sheetLine: Keep the choice you made, one further doubtful week.
cells.verb: Holding together under weight no one asks about
cells.place: A stripped-down region where the shape shows and the content drops away

cells.tense: You are bracing for a difficulty that has not arrived and may not arrive.
cells.act: give one thing and take one thing, in balance
cells.ask: Pass something real to someone who is with you, then accept something real back at the same size. One out, one in, taken plainly. Then stop counting.
cells.core:
You're braced, running the hard version ahead of time, living in next week rather than this one. The strength is sound. What has slipped is that you've stopped drawing on anyone and started hauling everything alone, as if no one nearby could take a share. From outside it reads as grit. Up close, those closest to you have quit offering, and the weight hasn't changed.

There's a way to hand it back without a speech: one even exchange. Give a thing away at its true size, then let something come back at that same size. Take it plainly — no tally kept, no talk about fairness. Two people passing weight between them is the point, not a debt done or owed. What you can't carry by yourself still gets carried once the traffic runs both ways.
cells.sheetLine: You're hauling what could be shared with those near you.

cells.tense: You are still stationed at a door that has already shut behind you.
cells.act: do the giving in the open this time, where it was always done unseen
cells.ask: Move one piece of the quiet work you do for someone into the open, where they can see it happen. Add no explanation. Once is enough.
cells.core:
The work continues, but all of it is spent honouring something that already closed. You keep a private observance going well after the thing it honours has ended, and because nobody sees it, it has no edge — no line that would mark it finished, so it doesn't finish. It's heavy and it registers nowhere. That isn't a fault in the endurance; the endurance is doing what it did before. What it lacks is daylight.

What stays hidden can't close. Let one piece of what you gave up, or keep giving, be visible one time — where whoever it was for can see it, with nothing explained and no story about old sacrifices. That much light is what a completed thing needs. Letting go is not a defeat; it's what finishing feels like once it's allowed into the open.
cells.sheetLine: What you gave up is real, and it can be seen once.

cells.tense: You are doing the standing right now, and your own account of it leaves your hand out.
cells.act: keep following the star after everything that has happened
cells.ask: Keep going after what you're actually pursuing through the next stretch, whatever came apart around it. Once, briefly, say in your own words that your hand is on it.
cells.core:
The persisting is real, and it belongs to you. Questioned, you'd credit circumstances, or stubbornness, or say anyone in your place would do the same. The pattern you read so precisely in other matters runs straight through your own hands, and none of the credit gets routed back. This is the earlier, plainer form of the same strength: not analysis, just the going. Each stretch that hasn't quit is a stretch you took, quietly, while looking at the obstacles rather than at what you were doing.

Nobody else needs telling. Take the next leg of what you're already pursuing, exactly as you've been pursuing it — one more stretch of the same heading after everything that has happened. Once, briefly, acknowledge in your own voice that the hand on it is yours. Not a label, not a medal. Just the plain fact, said plainly.
cells.sheetLine: The hand on what's still holding is yours.

attempts.check: The record supports a private endurance under material pressure, but not that the person is currently in hardship, and not how long or at what cost — so no cell may say what happened or name a duration. A reader could reasonably say the holding is simply steady and needs no adjustment; every cell therefore treats the pattern-sight as the thing bending, not the strength itself, and leaves the strength intact. Each ask survives being wrong because it is an act, not a diagnosis: if the read misses, the person still ends the week with one pattern seen, one debt settled, one gift witnessed, or one star followed. The sentence that serves me rather than them is the abstract 'seeing how things work underneath' line — it flatters the reader of the card, so it stays out of all four cores.
